title: Lemma-splitting: one hard equality into two helper lemmas joined by rw
intent: Reduce one hard equality A = C to two simpler equalities A = B and B = C by introducing an intermediate term B, then close the parent with the single rewrite chain `rw [lemma1, lemma2]`, so the parent is fully proved and only two smaller, independent holes remain.
also_known_as: move sorries earlier in the file

children.name: lemma1
children.statement: theorem lemma1 : A = B := by sorry
children.closed_by: sorry (left as a placeholder; the move deliberately defers this hole)

children.name: lemma2
children.statement: theorem lemma2 : B = C := by sorry
children.closed_by: sorry (left as a placeholder; the move deliberately defers this hole)

applicability.goal_shape: A goal that is an equality A = C (or another relation that `rw` composes) where a natural intermediate term B makes A = B and B = C each easier than A = C; the parent is then closed by a rewrite chain `rw [lemma1, lemma2]`.
applicability.use_when: there is a natural intermediate B (a definitional unfolding, a canonical or normal form, the midpoint of a calculation) that splits the goal into two lemmas each simpler than the whole; or when you want to work top-down and prove the target theorem first, leaving the helpers as `sorry`.
applicability.avoid_when: no such B exists (the two halves would be as hard as the whole); the two helper lemmas are not independent (one needs the other, so the chain gives no real split); or the goal is not an equality/transitive relation that `rw` composes.

claims.claim: In the After block the parent `main_theorem : A = C` is closed by the single tactic `rw [lemma1, lemma2]` (line 43), and the parent's two lines (42-43) contain no `sorry`; the only two `sorry`s in the After block are the helper lemmas `lemma1 : A = B` (line 40) and `lemma2 : B = C` (line 41).

The skill states the move and its reason in its own words: "Move sorries earlier in the file by replacing a `sorry` proof with references to simpler lemmas:" (line 33), motivated by "Go directly to the target theorem. Don't fill in `sorry`s in helper lemmas first — Lean treats `sorry` as an axiom, so dependent theorems still work." (line 31).

Counting `sorry` in the example: the Before state has one `sorry` on the whole goal (line 37); the After state has two (lines 40-41), each on an equality between adjacent terms, and the parent (lines 42-43) has none.

metrics.how_counted: counted from the Before/After example in the copied file, lines 36-44: the Before parent (line 37) has one sorry; the After block adds two helper lemmas (lines 40-41) each with one sorry; the After parent (lines 42-43) is one tactic with no sorry.

consequences: Creates two new top-level lemmas (`lemma1`, `lemma2`) that must eventually be proved or left as `sorry`. The parent's proof now depends on the intermediate `B` and on the rewrite chain composing (transitivity): `rw [lemma1]` rewrites A to B, then `rw [lemma2]` rewrites B to C. The move closes nothing by itself — it relocates one hole into two, and is only a win if each new hole is genuinely simpler. Failure mode: if `B` is not equal to `A` and `C` via the stated lemmas, `rw [lemma1, lemma2]` fails at the first link that does not apply.
